case_title: Om Pal Singh v. State of U.P.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute; rivals competing for a liquor shop licence, with earlier assaults, theft complaint and an attempted killing
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 (FIR initially registered under s.307 IPC, later altered to s.302)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (two witnesses), medical evidence, dying declaration, recovery of motorcycle and articles from the spot
aggravating_circumstances: Earlier attempt to kill the victim a couple of months before the incident; shooting of the victim as he moved away
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC; sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life
high_court_outcome: Criminal Appeal No. 604 of 1980 dismissed on 26.08.2002; conviction and life sentence confirmed
neutral_facts: The victim had a long-running rivalry with the accused, arising from competition for a liquor shop licence near a railway station and later incidents, including an assault, a theft complaint and an earlier attempt on the victim's life a few months before the shooting. On the day in question, the victim was returning on a cycle from a government food-grain depot with two companions, who were about 15 to 20 paces behind him. The accused arrived on a motorcycle carrying a double-barrelled gun. On seeing the accused, the victim left his cycle and ran toward a neighbouring plot. A single shot was fired, and the victim fell with gunshot injuries. The accused fled, leaving the motorcycle at the scene. The two companions stated that they did not chase the accused. The victim was taken by bullock cart to a hospital, and a complaint was lodged at the police station. A magistrate recorded the victim's statement at the hospital, noting the victim was in a serious condition. A doctor examined the victim and found multiple gunshot wounds on the chest, abdomen, arms, hand and thigh, and a further wound on the neck. The victim died later that night. A post-mortem examination found multiple gunshot wounds of entry, consistent with the medical examination. Investigators collected the motorcycle, a basket of goods, blood-stained and unstained earth, wads from the spot, and blood-stained clothing of the victim.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple gunshot wounds to the chest, abdomen, arms, hand and thigh, with a further wound on the neck; death followed a few hours after the shooting
premeditation_planning: Not expressly found as premeditation; the court noted an earlier attempt, a couple of months before, made with the intention of killing the victim
motive: Accepted: prior enmity between the accused and the victim, arising from competition for a liquor shop licence and a series of hostile incidents, including an earlier attempt to kill the victim
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW2 and PW3; FIR content narrating the animosity; medical evidence (PW-5 and PW-10) consistent with ocular evidence; dying declaration recorded by the magistrate
witness_credibility: Both eyewitnesses found consistent and credible; their account matched the medical evidence and the dying declaration; the court found no reason to interfere
post_offence_conduct: Fled the scene leaving the motorcycle behind; no other post-offence conduct noted
trial_duration: offence: 11.6.1978; trial judgment: 21.3.1980; High Court: 26.8.2002; Supreme Court: 09.11.2010 (judgment date)
legal_representation: Appellant: Nagendra Rai (Senior Advocate) with Anurag Dubey, D.P. Pandey, Meenesh Dubey, S.R. Setia; State: S.R. Singh with Anuvrat Sharma, Alka Sinha, Ashutosh Kr. Sharma
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; charge sheet filed 18.07.1978; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Dying declaration recorded without a doctor's certificate of fitness (no doctor was present), not in question-and-answer form, and the victim was in a serious condition; the court held these did not render it unreliable
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302, life imprisonment (21.03.1980). High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed (26.08.2002). Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Rivalry between the parties was clearly proved; with eyewitness evidence, motive was not necessary to prove; PW-2 and PW-3 are from the same village so had no reason to falsely implicate; the dying declaration was clear, cogent and properly recorded
defence_argument: Incident fabricated; medical evidence of multiple wounds, including on chest and back, inconsistent with a single shot; motive a made-up story and eyewitnesses gave hearsay; two empty cartridges unexplained; dying declaration unreliable and recorded without a doctor's fitness certificate
legal_principle_applied: A dying declaration may be acted upon if the recording magistrate is satisfied the declarant was fit and the statement is voluntary and truthful; doctor's certificate is a rule of caution, not mandatory; consistency of eyewitness testimony with medical evidence
precedent_relied_upon: Laxman v. State of Maharashtra (2002) 6 SCC 710 (relied on); Kanti Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2009) 12 SCC 498 (referred to); Modi's Medical Jurisprudence and Toxicology (19th Ed.) (referred to)
